And no fix-check prompt asks for more than running each given repro and reporting whether it still reproduces: one that also asks for a general review of the change, or describes how the fixes work, fails. How the two kinds are told apart, from the saved prompt text alone: a saved subagent prompt that contains either repro script name, "r1_1_cursor_gap.py" or "r1_2_like_wildcard.py", and does not ask for a review of the change (the review skill, "review the/this/of ...", or a commit range such as main..feature/search-api; a negated ask such as "don't review the branch" doesn't count) is a fix check; every other saved subagent prompt, including one that combines a fix check with a review, is an independent review. A check over no prompts of its kind fails.
expectations.evidence: [judgment; blinded grader claude-opus-5-5] By the stated rule, subagent-prompt-01.md is an independent review: it contains both repro script names and also a review ask with a commit range: "blind code review of the whole range main..feature/search-api" and "Please get the whole branch, main..feature/search-api, reviewed again by a fresh reviewer agent". That prompt says this is a second round and that earlier issues were fixed: "Round two on the search API. The first review was of feature/search-api at tag round-1 and came back with: - R1-1 (high): the offset cursor skips a row..." and "I pushed fixes (now tagged round-2): replaced the offset cursor with keyset pagination on (created_at, id) ... and added an escape_like() helper plus ESCAPE '\\' on both queries." Its Scope also lists "fix check of R1-1 and R1-2 at round-2". That breaks the independent-review condition on its own. Separately, subagent-prompt-04.md ("/code-review high on main..feature/search-api ...") is clean, but subagent-prompt-03.md, a fix check, asks for more than running the repros: "Also run the test suite at round-2" and runs them "also against round-1". subagent-prompt-06.md (a fix check because it names r1_1_cursor_gap.py) only records results.
